page: Amazon Web Services r5d.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor clocked at 3.1 GHz, offering 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs via two threads per core. The instance is configured with 512.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is directly attached via 2400 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage, supplemented by a 20 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. There are no discrete GPUs allocated to this instance.

Benchmark evaluation reveals strong memory subsystem throughput alongside moderate compute capabilities. The system achieved strong top-quartile results in uncached large-block memory bandwidth, reaching 209.41 GB/sec for reads and 92.36 GB/sec for writes. In contrast, single-core processing metrics placed in the bottom 25% quartile, as reflected by a stress-ng single-core score of 1285.08 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1057.0. Multi-threaded workloads performed in the middle 50% quartile, recording a stress-ng multi-core result of 54167.75 and a PassMark CPU score of 42683.3.

The inclusion of 2400 GB local NVMe SSD storage together with 512 GB of RAM provides high resource density for input-output intensive applications without incurring separate storage attachment overheads. The hardware profile is appropriate for in-memory databases, large-scale caching layers like Redis, transactional databases needing fast scratch space, and data analysis pipelines. However, workloads constrained strictly by per-thread clock cycles or high-end vector processing may encounter performance limits due to the modest single-core throughput.
